title: Seerah
description: A question bank on the life of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), covering revelation, migration, community life, major events and lessons, with explanations and primary-text references.
difficultyMethod: Editorial classification; not calibrated from learner response data. Advanced means greater reasoning depth within this subject, not a scholarly qualification.

review.referenceCheck: Primary-text references checked during preparation; this is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Handle I am not sure as a UI action, not as a fifth answer option.

questions.question: In which cave did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) receive the opening revelation described in Sahih al-Bukhari 3?

options.text: Hira
Thawr
The Cave of the Sleepers
A cave near Jerusalem

questions.explanation: The first-revelation account places the encounter in Hira, where he had been spending time in worship.

questions.question: Who reassured the Prophet after his first encounter with revelation?

options.text: Hafsah
Khadijah
Umm Salamah
Aishah

questions.explanation: Khadijah comforted him and recalled his care for relatives, vulnerable people and guests.

questions.question: Whom did Khadijah consult about the Prophet's experience of revelation?

options.text: Abu Lahab
Abu Jahl
Waraqah ibn Nawfal
Suraqah ibn Malik

questions.explanation: Khadijah took him to Waraqah, her cousin, who had knowledge of earlier scripture.

questions.question: At approximately what age did the Prophet begin receiving revelation?

options.text: Twenty
Thirty
Sixty
Forty

questions.explanation: Anas's description in Sahih al-Bukhari 3547 places the beginning of revelation at forty years of age.

questions.question: From which place did the Prophet call Quraysh when warning his close relatives?

options.text: Al-Safa
Mount Uhud
The plain of Arafat
The valley of Mina

questions.explanation: The narration of the public warning describes him ascending Al-Safa and calling the clans of Quraysh.

questions.question: To which city did the Prophet migrate from Makkah?

options.text: Taif
Madinah
Jerusalem
Alexandria

questions.explanation: The Hijrah account describes his departure from Makkah and arrival in Madinah.

questions.question: Who accompanied the Prophet in the cave during the migration?

options.text: Umar
Uthman
Abu Bakr
Ali

questions.explanation: Abu Bakr narrates his concern while with the Prophet in the cave and the Prophet's reassurance.

questions.question: Who prepared provisions and used part of her waistband to tie them for the migration journey?

options.text: Fatimah bint Muhammad
Umm Ayman
Safiyyah bint Huyayy
Asma bint Abi Bakr

questions.explanation: The migration account identifies Asma's practical help with the travellers' provisions.

questions.question: At whose home did the Prophet dismount on arriving in the central settlement of Madinah?

options.text: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
Abu Lahab
Heraclius
Waraqah ibn Nawfal

questions.explanation: Anas's arrival account describes the Prophet dismounting in the courtyard of Abu Ayyub's home.

questions.question: In Quran 9:100, which group is named alongside the Muhajirun among the early believers?

options.text: The Romans
The Ansar
The Persians
The people of Pharaoh

questions.explanation: The verse names the Muhajirun and Ansar. Ansar refers to the supporters from Madinah who helped the Muslim community.

questions.question: Which battle is explicitly named in Quran 3:123 as an occasion of Allah's help?

options.text: Uhud
Hunayn
Badr
Khaybar

questions.explanation: Ali Imran 3:123 explicitly names Badr when reminding believers of Allah's help.

questions.question: At Uhud, which companion commanded the archers whom the Prophet stationed at a designated position?

options.text: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
Zayd ibn Thabit
Waraqah ibn Nawfal
Abdullah ibn Jubayr

questions.explanation: Al-Bara's account names Abdullah ibn Jubayr as the commander of the archers and records their instructions to remain at their post.

questions.question: Which agreement is described in Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732?

options.text: The treaty of Hudaybiyyah
A trade agreement with Persia
A pact made after the Prophet's death
A treaty between Musa and Pharaoh

questions.explanation: The extended narration describes the journey, negotiations and agreement at Hudaybiyyah.

questions.question: Who received the banner from the Prophet in the well-known Khaybar narration?

options.text: Abu Lahab
Ali ibn Abi Talib
Suraqah ibn Malik
Waraqah ibn Nawfal

questions.explanation: Sahl ibn Sad's narration identifies Ali as the recipient of the banner at Khaybar.

questions.question: Which companion's truthful account of missing Tabuk is narrated at length in Sahih al-Bukhari 4418?

options.text: Bilal ibn Rabah
Abu Dharr
Kab ibn Malik
Musab ibn Umayr

questions.explanation: Kab recounts his failure to join Tabuk, his truthful admission and the acceptance of his repentance.

questions.question: At the conquest of Makkah, what did the Prophet remove from around the Kabah?

options.text: Copies of the Quran
Palm trees planted by the Ansar
The walls of the Kabah
Idols

questions.explanation: Ibn Masud's narration describes the Prophet striking the idols around the Kabah while proclaiming the triumph of truth.

questions.question: What does the expression Hajjat al-Wada refer to?

options.text: The Farewell Pilgrimage
The migration to Abyssinia
The first revelation
The treaty of Hudaybiyyah

questions.explanation: The expression refers to the Prophet's Farewell Pilgrimage, described in pilgrimage narrations including Jabir's detailed account.

questions.question: Which son of the Prophet is named in the narration about his tears at a child's death?

options.text: Ismail
Ibrahim
Yusuf
Yahya

questions.explanation: Anas describes the death of the Prophet's son Ibrahim and the Prophet's tears of mercy and grief.

questions.question: According to Aishah, what did the Prophet do at home?

options.text: Refuse all household tasks
Spend every moment receiving official visitors
Help with his family's work
Require guests to do all domestic work

questions.explanation: Aishah describes him serving his family and going out when the call to prayer was heard.

questions.question: How did the Prophet continue to honour Khadijah's friendships after her death?

options.text: He forbade anyone to mention her.
He demanded that her friends leave Madinah.
He treated loyalty to her as unnecessary.
He sent portions of meat to her friends.

questions.explanation: Aishah recalls his frequent remembrance of Khadijah and his gifts to her women friends.

questions.question: Who reviewed the Quran with the Prophet in Ramadan?

options.text: Jibril
Heraclius
Abu Lahab
The ruler of Persia

questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas describes Jibril meeting the Prophet in Ramadan to study the Quran with him.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 4998, how many times was the Quran reviewed with the Prophet in the year of his death?

options.text: Once
Twice
Three times
Ten times

questions.explanation: Abu Hurayrah reports an annual review, with two reviews in the Prophet's final year.

questions.question: Which ruler received the Prophet's letter discussed in the narration of Abu Sufyan's interview?

options.text: Pharaoh
The king in Yusuf's story
Heraclius
Dhul-Qarnayn

questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari 7 records Heraclius questioning Abu Sufyan and hearing the Prophet's letter.

questions.question: Which childhood circumstance is recalled in Quran 93:6 when addressing the Prophet?

options.text: Growing up as a reigning king
Commanding an army as a child
Owning the treasury of Persia
Being an orphan

questions.explanation: Ad-Duha 93:6 recalls Allah finding him an orphan and giving him shelter.

questions.question: In Quran 2:144, toward which sacred place is the Prophet instructed to turn in prayer?

options.text: Al-Masjid al-Haram
Mount Sinai
The palace of Heraclius
The cave of Hira

questions.explanation: Al-Baqarah 2:144 records the instruction to turn toward Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questions.question: Which destination is named alongside Al-Masjid al-Haram in Quran 17:1's account of the night journey?

options.text: The mosque of Quba
Al-Masjid al-Aqsa
Mount Uhud
The valley of Hunayn

questions.explanation: Al-Isra 17:1 names the journey from Al-Masjid al-Haram to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa.

questions.question: Which battle is named in Quran 9:25 when explaining that large numbers did not by themselves ensure success?

options.text: Badr
Tabuk
Hunayn
Khaybar

questions.explanation: At-Tawbah 9:25 names Hunayn and recalls that the believers' impressive numbers did not initially benefit them.

questions.question: Which uncle opposed the Prophet's warning at Al-Safa in the narration of Sahih al-Bukhari 4770?

options.text: Hamzah
Al-Abbas
Abu Talib
Abu Lahab

questions.explanation: The narration records Abu Lahab's hostile response to the public warning.

questions.question: After arriving in Madinah, which prophet's deliverance was mentioned in the account of fasting on Ashura?

options.text: Musa
Yusuf
Dawud
Sulayman

questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas's account connects the observed fast with Allah granting Musa and the Israelites deliverance from Pharaoh.

questions.question: According to Aishah's answer in Sahih al-Bukhari 1387, on which day of the week did the Prophet die?

options.text: Friday
Monday
Saturday
Thursday

questions.explanation: Aishah's answer identifies Monday as the day of the Prophet's death. This question does not ask for a disputed calendar date.

questions.question: Why did Khadijah's reassurance after the first revelation involve more than a general expression of sympathy?

options.text: She claimed kindness removed any need for revelation.
She promised he would never face opposition.
She pointed to his established care for people as grounds for confidence in Allah's help.
She said public wealth was the only sign of divine favour.

questions.explanation: Her reassurance recalled concrete qualities of character, including maintaining family ties and helping people in distress.

questions.question: The migration account mentions preparations, provisions and a hired guide. Which conclusion fits these details?

options.text: Trust in Allah required rejecting every practical precaution.
A guide replaced the need for trust in Allah.
Planning meant the travellers were certain no danger existed.
Trust in Allah was accompanied by practical planning.

questions.explanation: The account presents purposeful arrangements alongside reliance on Allah; these are not treated as opposites.

questions.question: What best captures the Prophet's response when Abu Bakr feared discovery in the cave?

options.text: Reassurance grounded in Allah's presence and support
A claim that no pursuer had come near them
An instruction to abandon belief because of danger
A promise that no believer would ever feel afraid again

questions.explanation: The narration records reassurance in a real moment of danger, rather than denying the existence of that danger.

questions.question: What made the archers' departure from their position at Uhud a failure to follow the Prophet's instruction?

options.text: He had ordered them to follow the first person who left.
He had told them to remain even if the battle appeared to turn decisively.
He had given no instructions about leaving.
He had made collecting spoils their only responsibility.

questions.explanation: The order covered contrasting battlefield outcomes, so apparent success did not cancel it.

questions.question: At Hudaybiyyah, how did Umm Salamah help when the companions were slow to act on the instruction to end ihram?

options.text: She advised abandoning the agreement secretly.
She instructed the companions to invent a new pilgrimage ritual.
She advised the Prophet to go out and perform the actions himself.
She said consultation had no place in resolving the difficulty.

questions.explanation: The narration describes her practical advice and the companions following the Prophet's example once he acted.

questions.question: What distinguished Kab ibn Malik's explanation for not joining Tabuk?

options.text: He blamed a journey he had never taken.
He claimed illness despite knowing he was healthy.
He denied that he had been expected to join.
He admitted that he had no valid excuse instead of inventing one.

questions.explanation: Kab's account centres on truthful admission despite the immediate difficulty it brought.

questions.question: After severe rejection, the angel of the mountains offered to crush the people between the mountains. How did the Prophet respond?

options.text: He hoped their descendants would worship Allah alone.
He demanded that all their descendants also be destroyed.
He declared that no one from their community could ever believe.
He accepted destruction because every rejection required it.

questions.explanation: Aishah's narration records a response of restraint and hope rather than the offered destruction.

questions.question: What does the Prophet's response to Ibrahim's death show about grief?

options.text: Faith makes every tear a sign of disbelief.
Tears and sadness can coexist with speech that pleases Allah.
Parents must pretend they feel no loss.
Grief requires speaking resentfully about Allah.

questions.explanation: The narration joins heartfelt sorrow with restraint in what is said.

questions.question: Aishah says the Prophet chose the easier of two matters. What condition is essential to that description?

options.text: The easier option always brought more money.
The easier option had to impress the largest crowd.
The easier option did not involve sin.
The easier option could ignore every religious limit.

questions.explanation: The narration explicitly limits this preference to choices that were not sinful.

questions.question: According to Aishah's description, how did the Prophet deal with personal injury or offence?

options.text: He always retaliated more harshly than the injury.
He treated every personal slight as a reason for warfare.
He allowed anger to replace all religious limits.
He did not seek revenge merely for himself.

questions.explanation: Her description distinguishes personal revenge from the matter of Allah's limits being violated.

questions.question: In the Farewell Pilgrimage address reported by Jabir, which responsibilities toward women were emphasized?

options.text: Treating them with awareness of Allah and providing food and clothing appropriately
Treating financial care as unnecessary
Making harshness the measure of family leadership
Withholding basic care whenever convenient

questions.explanation: The address includes concrete obligations of care, rather than reducing family responsibility to a title.

questions.question: What responsibility did the Prophet give those present in the Farewell Pilgrimage address reported by Abu Bakrah?

options.text: Keep the address secret from later Muslims.
Convey the message to those who were absent.
Pass it on only if they added a new story.
Assume no absent person could understand it.

questions.explanation: The address directs those present to transmit what they heard and notes that a later recipient may understand it well.

questions.question: Quran 3:159 describes gentleness and consultation in the Prophet's leadership. What outcome does it associate with harshness?

options.text: People would automatically become more sincere.
Consultation would become unnecessary.
People would have dispersed from around him.
Every disagreement would disappear.

questions.explanation: The verse connects merciful conduct with community cohesion and instructs consultation.

questions.question: What did the Prophet's participation in building the mosque after arriving in Madinah demonstrate?

options.text: A refusal to take part in ordinary labour
A rule that only visitors could build places of worship
An instruction to postpone all community life indefinitely
Shared practical work in establishing the community

questions.explanation: Anas's arrival narration describes the mosque's construction and the Prophet joining in carrying building materials.

questions.question: In the Khaybar banner narration, what instruction accompanied the mission given to Ali?

options.text: Invite the people to Islam and explain their duties toward Allah.
Treat guidance as less important than personal recognition.
Assume no explanation of the message was needed.
Promise that worldly payment alone would establish belief.

questions.explanation: The narration highlights invitation and guidance, including the value of one person being guided.

questions.question: Some companions found the Hudaybiyyah terms difficult to accept. What is the soundest lesson about evaluating the agreement?

options.text: Every agreement that feels difficult must be rejected.
Immediate discomfort did not by itself establish that the Prophet's decision was mistaken.
The companions' distress proved they had no faith at all.
Any later leader's treaty must automatically have the same authority as a prophetic decision.

questions.explanation: The account records genuine distress alongside the Prophet's commitment to the agreement. The lesson does not make every later political decision infallible.

questions.question: In the Hudaybiyyah account, Abu Jandal's arrival created an especially painful test. Which tension is central to understanding the episode?

options.text: A disagreement over whether prayer existed
A choice between two unrelated trade routes
Concern for a persecuted believer alongside commitment to negotiated terms
A dispute about who had memorized more poetry

questions.explanation: The episode must be read within the negotiations and the Prophet's response, rather than reduced to indifference toward suffering.

questions.question: Kab's repentance was not followed by immediate public relief. Which conclusion avoids misreading his account?

options.text: Repentance is genuine only when consequences end the same day.
His honesty guaranteed that no discipline could follow.
The delay proved that Allah never accepts serious repentance.
A period of painful waiting did not mean that truthful repentance was pointless.

questions.explanation: His narrative ends with acceptance after a difficult interval, distinguishing sincere repentance from instant removal of consequences.

questions.question: During Kab's isolation, a foreign ruler offered him an alternative allegiance. Why is his rejection significant in the narrative?

options.text: He refused an apparently attractive escape that would compromise his loyalty.
He proved that every letter from outside Arabia was forged.
He established that reading any foreign correspondence was forbidden.
He showed that isolation removes all moral responsibility.

questions.explanation: Kab recognized the invitation as another trial and destroyed the letter rather than using it to escape the consequences of his failure.

questions.question: Someone argues that the conquest gave everyone a permanent licence to fight in Makkah. What distinction did the Prophet expressly make?

options.text: The conquest permanently ended the city's sacred status.
His exceptional permission was limited and did not remove Makkah's continuing sanctity.
Any person could claim the same exception without evidence.
The city's sanctity depended entirely on a later ruler's preference.

questions.explanation: Abu Shurayh's report warns against generalizing the Prophet's exceptional permission into an unrestricted licence.

questions.question: What conclusion goes beyond the report about the Prophet's restraint after rejection near Taif?

options.text: That he declined the offered destruction
That he hoped for future generations who would worship Allah
That the report alone proves there can never be any lawful response to wrongdoing in any circumstance
That rejection did not eliminate his concern for people's guidance

questions.explanation: The report demonstrates a particular act of mercy. Turning it into a universal legal conclusion without considering other evidence exceeds what this episode alone establishes.

questions.question: Someone says public religious leadership made household service beneath the Prophet's dignity. Which response best uses Aishah's report?

options.text: The report proves household work was his only activity.
The report says only people without public responsibilities should help.
The report makes service to family incompatible with worship.
His own practice directly challenges the claim: he served his family and attended prayer.

questions.explanation: Aishah's description places domestic service and worship within the same daily life, undermining the claimed conflict.

questions.question: A social-media post combines several farewell-address reports into one long quotation. What is the most accurate way to present it?

options.text: Identify the sources for each passage and label a combined presentation as a compilation.
Attribute every sentence to one hadith number without checking.
Assume all popular versions have identical wording.
Add inspiring sentences and keep quotation marks around the whole text.

questions.explanation: Jabir and Abu Bakrah transmit distinct reports. A compiled summary must not be presented as the exact uninterrupted wording of one narration.

questions.question: At Al-Safa, the audience acknowledged the Prophet's truthfulness before some rejected his warning. What does this distinction show?

options.text: Every listener immediately accepted Islam.
Acknowledging someone's honesty does not necessarily mean accepting the message they bring.
The audience said he had always been dishonest.
The warning concerned only a military attack and had no religious purpose.

questions.explanation: The narration distinguishes recognition of his truthful character from the subsequent response to his warning.

questions.question: Quran 3:159 joins pardon, seeking forgiveness, consultation and reliance on Allah. Which leadership response best reflects this combination after a setback?

options.text: Treat a setback as permission to abandon all consultation.
Assume mercy prevents any decision from being made.
Address failures while maintaining mercy, consultation and trust in Allah.
Replace reliance on Allah with confidence in numbers alone.

questions.explanation: The verse holds these responsibilities together; none cancels the others.

questions.question: How does Quran 9:25 correct the assumption that numerical superiority guarantees success?

options.text: It states that preparing resources is always forbidden.
It claims the believers never felt fear.
It makes defeat proof that every member of a community is insincere.
It recalls that impressive numbers at Hunayn did not initially protect the believers.

questions.explanation: The verse challenges reliance on numbers as a guarantee. It does not abolish practical preparation or authorize judging every person's sincerity.

questions.question: Quran 59:9 praises the receiving community's generosity even amid need. Which conclusion best preserves the point of this praise?

options.text: Their support involved real preference for others despite personal need.
They were generous only because they had no needs of their own.
The passage praises envy of the newcomers' gifts.
It says the newcomers needed no assistance.

questions.explanation: The verse describes affection for the emigrants and generosity despite need, giving substance to the idea of support.

questions.question: The final-year report says the Quran was reviewed twice and the Prophet's itikaf lasted twenty days. Which claim is directly supported?

options.text: Every Muslim must perform twenty days of itikaf every year.
His final year included an increased review and a longer retreat than his usual annual practice.
The Quran was reviewed only after the Prophet's death.
The report gives an exact date for the first revelation.

questions.explanation: The narration reports his practice. A universal obligation or an unrelated historical date cannot be established merely from these details.

questions.question: After the Prophet's death, Quran 3:144 was recited in the account of Abu Bakr's address. Which distinction was central?

options.text: The Messenger's death made every previous teaching false.
The community could no longer worship Allah.
The Messenger's death does not mean that Allah dies or that worship of Allah ends.
All messengers had been exempt from death.

questions.explanation: The report recalls Abu Bakr redirecting the community to Allah and reciting the verse about the Messenger's mortality.

questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders these major events in the Prophet's life?

options.text: Migration to Madinah, first revelation, Farewell Pilgrimage, Hudaybiyyah
Hudaybiyyah, first revelation, migration to Madinah, Farewell Pilgrimage
Farewell Pilgrimage, Hudaybiyyah, migration to Madinah, first revelation
First revelation, migration to Madinah, Hudaybiyyah, Farewell Pilgrimage

questions.explanation: The first revelation belongs to the Makkan period; migration begins the Madinan period; Hudaybiyyah precedes the Farewell Pilgrimage. The linked reports document these distinct stages.
